_note: BASELINE-v2 — the first English measurement on a holdout proven disjoint from training. Supersedes every figure derived from multilingual/test/en_holdout.csv, which was 1460/1461 training rows (Review-F5 blocker B9).
_grade_note: Authoritative, not provisional: datasets/ is the byte-exact tree recovered from git (29 files, 7072263 bytes, matching the retired DVC pointer), not the English bootstrap snapshot.

conditions.temperature_provenance: FITTED out-of-fold by nlu_training.fit_calibration (charter B2); provenance in models/intent/en/calibration.json. Replaces the stale device value 0.796286 that blocker B8 identified.

superseded_baseline.why_invalid: 1460 of 1461 rows appear verbatim in the training data

finding: Accuracy barely moved (0.9007 vs 0.907) but ECE is 2.4x worse (0.0441 vs 0.018). The leakage was not inflating ACCURACY — it was concealing MISCALIBRATION. Confidence looked trustworthy because it was measured on memorised phrases. Every confidence-gated behaviour (the 0.70 fire threshold, the 0.80 confirm gate, semantic rescue) was tuned against that illusion, which is exactly what B2/B3 fix.

calibration_fix.note: T is rank-preserving, so accuracy is identical to 4dp by construction — only the confidence scale moved. ECE on the honest holdout improved 1.4x. On the out-of-fold fitting distribution the improvement is 11.8x (0.1170 -> 0.0099); the holdout figure is the honest out-of-sample one and is the one to quote.

amendments.what: Relabelled 5 utterances wrongly marked sys.oos.fallback where an in-scope sibling made the label a contradiction (scripts/ci/fix_oos_mislabels.py): 3x 'read last text message' -> messaging.message.listen, 'translate hello to french' -> translation.session.start, 'where do i find the mute button' -> help.volume.show. 4 rows in train.csv, 1 in holdout_honest.csv. The train/holdout PARTITION is unchanged, so the sets remain disjoint — this is a label correction, not a re-split.
amendments.note: All three metrics improved and ECE nearly halved (0.0315 -> 0.0178). Five contradictory labels were costing more than their count suggests: an utterance labelled out-of-scope while its paraphrase is in-scope puts conflicting pressure on that intent's decision boundary, which shows up as miscalibration rather than as error.
